note: Itiner-e static version 2024 (Zenodo 17122148, v1.3): 14,769 digitised road sections of the Roman Empire, c. 300 BC–AD 300. Certainty grades the spatial accuracy of the drawn course: 'certain' = well documented, within 50 m (mountains) or 200 m (plains); 'conjectured' = road known, course less precisely documented; 'hypothetical' = road identified but not localised, tracks not fixed (deserts, flood plains), or speculated. Orbis joined sections end to end, simplified them (Douglas-Peucker, about 2 km for main and 5 km for secondary roads) and rounded to 0.01°. Lengths ('km') are sums of the dataset's geodesic Shape_Leng before simplification.
